# Installing claude-toolkit

Instructions for a developer, or for Claude Code acting for one. Follow the steps in order, run the verification at the end of each step, and stop and report if a step fails. Do not change anything not listed here.

There are two parts. Install **Part 1** for the session view; add **Part 2** only if you want the coordinator workflow.

| Part | What you get | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Claude sessions | "Claude sessions" view with colour-coded status of every Claude session, status-bar count, `Ctrl+Alt+N` to jump to waiting sessions, click to focus a session in any VS Code window, `STATUS:` line in every session, optional automatic Claude tab when a folder opens | VS Code extension link + status hooks |
| 2. Coordinator | A coordinator session per project that creates and briefs worker sessions | Part 1 + enabling the coordinator per folder |

## Prerequisites

Check each one and stop if it is missing:

- VS Code: `code --version`
- Claude Code CLI on `PATH`: `claude --version`
- Node.js 20 or newer: `node --version`
- Git, with read access to `github.com/dserri/claude-toolkit` (private: ask its owner for access): `git ls-remote https://github.com/dserri/claude-toolkit.git`

## Part 1: Claude sessions

### 1.1 Clone

Clone into a stable folder; the hooks and the extension point at it, so do not move it afterwards. Below, `<clone>` is that absolute path.

```
git clone https://github.com/dserri/claude-toolkit.git <clone>
```

Verify: `<clone>/vscode/package.json` and `<clone>/status/install.mjs` exist.

### 1.2 Link the VS Code extension

Windows (PowerShell):

```
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.vscode\extensions\dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1" -Target "<clone>\vscode"
```

macOS / Linux:

```
ln -s "<clone>/vscode" ~/.vscode/extensions/dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1
```

Verify: `code --list-extensions --show-versions` lists `dserri.claude-toolkit@0.0.1`.

### 1.3 Install the status hooks

```
node <clone>/status/install.mjs
```

It backs up `~/.claude/settings.json` (printing the backup path) and adds only its own hook entries; existing settings and hooks stay unchanged. Running it again changes nothing.

Verify: `~/.claude/settings.json` has entries running `status-hook.mjs` (marked `"async": true`) for `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, and one `SessionStart` entry running `turn-status-hook.mjs`.

### 1.4 Reload VS Code

In every open VS Code window: Command Palette → "Developer: Reload Window". Claude sessions already running are not tracked until restarted; new ones are.

Verify, with the developer:
- The Activity Bar (left icon strip) shows a "Claude sessions" icon (three stacked bars). To place it under the Explorer, drag it there once; VS Code remembers the order for all windows.
- The status bar shows `none waiting` or `N waiting`.
- A new Claude session (`claude` in a terminal) appears as a card within seconds and ends its turns with `STATUS: DONE` or `STATUS: QUESTION`.

### 1.5 Optional: open Claude automatically in a folder

Open the project folder, then Command Palette → "Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup". A `claude` tab opens now and every time VS Code opens that folder. To resume an earlier conversation in it, use `/resume`. "Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" turns it off.

## Part 2: Coordinator (optional)

Requires Part 1. In the project folder: Command Palette → "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder on this machine, creates `.coord/` (excluded from Git through `.git/info/exclude`) and opens a `coordinator` tab. From then on the coordinator opens with the folder; tell it the goal and it creates worker tabs. See README.md for how it works. Sessions load the toolkit plugin from the clone automatically; no plugin install is needed.

## Settings

All machine-scoped, under `claudeToolkit.` in VS Code settings:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `workerLayout` | `beside` | Coordinator workers open beside the coordinator, or `tabs` for full-width tabs |
| `stuckMinutes` | `15` | Minutes without events before a working session shows as possibly stuck (read-only tool calls such as Read or Grep produce no events) |
| `claudePath` | `claude` from `PATH` | Claude Code executable |
| `pluginDir` | `<clone>/plugins/toolkit` | Toolkit plugin folder (coordinator only) |

## Updating

```
git -C <clone> pull
node <clone>/status/install.mjs
```

Re-running the installer after a pull is required whenever the hook entries change; it replaces only the toolkit's own entries.

Then reload VS Code windows.

## Uninstalling

```
node <clone>/status/install.mjs --uninstall
```

Then delete the extension link (`~/.vscode/extensions/dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1`), reload VS Code, and optionally delete `~/.agent-status/`. "Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" before uninstalling removes a folder's automatic start.

## Troubleshooting

- **No cards appear:** the session was started before the hooks were installed (restart it), or the folder's workspace trust was not accepted (Claude Code runs hooks only in trusted folders). Hook errors are logged to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`.
- **Headless sessions** (`claude -p`, SDK, SDD's reviewer) are skipped on purpose.
- **Windows Terminal windows flashing during SDD checks** come from SDD 0.3.0-rc.47 and later (check commands started without a hidden window), not from this toolkit; a fix has been requested from the SDD maintainer.

# claude-toolkit

Personal Claude Code plugins, laid out as a private plugin marketplace. A proof of concept: it is compatible with the team-shared SDD skill but entirely separate from it, and never changes it. Every toolkit agent carries the `toolkit:` prefix.

## What it does

Two parts, installable separately. **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) is the setup guide** (written so Claude Code can follow it for you).

1. **Claude sessions**: a "Claude sessions" view with the live, colour-coded status of every Claude session on the machine, a status-bar count, `Ctrl+Alt+N` to jump to waiting sessions, click-to-focus across VS Code windows, a `STATUS:` line at the end of every turn, and optionally a plain Claude tab that opens with a folder ("Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup"). Needs only the extension link and the status hooks.
2. **Coordinator**: open a project and a **coordinator** Claude session starts in an editor tab. It reports the SDD team recap, reads the project board and asks what is next. You tell it the goal; it creates the **worker** sessions the job needs, each in its own named tab with a written brief, and follows them through SendMessage. Workers that still have open work reopen with their conversation the next time you open the project. You can still type in any worker's tab.

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| Status hooks (session events, `STATUS:` line instruction) and their installer | `status/` |
| `toolkit:coordinator` and `toolkit:worker` agents | `plugins/toolkit/agents/` |
| Start-up hook: runs SDD's team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only | `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` |
| VS Code extension: session view, plain Claude tab, coordinator and worker tabs | `vscode/` |

One project per coordinator; coordinating several projects is planned.

## Coordinator sessions

The extension starts every coordinator and worker session with `--plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit` and `--permission-mode auto` (sessions in the same mode exchange messages without approval prompts). `claude` must be on `PATH`, or set `claudeToolkit.claudePath`; `claudeToolkit.pluginDir` overrides the plugin folder. `claudeToolkit.workerLayout` chooses where worker tabs open: `beside` (default, the column next to the coordinator) or `tabs` (full-width tabs in the coordinator's column).

## Enable a project

Open the project folder and run "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder as enabled on this machine (in the extension's own storage, never in the repository), creates `.coord/`, adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (never `.gitignore`), and opens the coordinator. From then on the coordinator opens whenever VS Code opens the folder; "Toolkit: Start coordinator" opens it again if you closed it. A repository that carries a `.coord/` folder starts nothing until you enable it yourself, and the extension's settings are machine-scoped, so a workspace cannot change which executable or plugin it runs.

### The board (`.coord/`)

| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `team.json` | coordinator | `[{ "name", "role", "state": "active" \| "done" }]`; active workers reopen at start-up |
| `workers/<name>/brief.md` | coordinator | the worker's task |
| `workers/<name>/status.md` | worker | `State`, `Summary`, `Next` |
| `requests/<name>.json` | coordinator | `{ "name": "<name>" }`: asks the extension to open the worker; rejected requests leave `<name>.rejected.md` |
| `log.md` | coordinator | decisions, assignments and outcomes |
| `sessions/<session name>.id` | start-up hook | each worker's session ID, so its tab resumes exactly its own conversation, also when the coordinator requests a finished worker again |

Sessions are named `<project>-coordinator` and `<project>-<worker>` (the project folder name in lowercase, other characters as hyphens); tabs show the short name. Enabled projects need different folder names, or their sessions share names.

## Session status

The "Claude sessions" view (its own icon in the Activity Bar, the same in every window; drag it elsewhere once if you prefer) and the status-bar item show every interactive Claude Code session on this machine, toolkit or not. Clicking the status-bar item (`🔔 2 waiting`) shows the session waiting longest; `Ctrl+Alt+N` ("Toolkit: Next waiting session") cycles through the waiting sessions in urgency order; both reach tabs in other windows like a card click does.

| Colour | Status | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| red | waiting for permission / waiting for your answer | `PermissionRequest`; `AskUserQuestion`, or a turn ending with `STATUS: QUESTION` (coordinator and worker) or a final `?` |
| purple | possibly stuck | working with no event for `claudeToolkit.stuckMinutes` (default 15; read-only tools such as Read and Grep record no event) |
| blue | working in background | the turn ended while background tasks (a dev server, a long command) still run; the card shows how many |
| yellow | finished, needs review | any other end of turn |
| green | working | a prompt or a tool result |
| grey | idle | session started, no prompt yet |

Cards are grouped by project folder (each group shows how many of its sessions wait). Drag sessions within their project, and projects among projects, to arrange the view; your order is kept in every window and wins over urgency, while sessions and projects you never placed follow yours sorted by urgency (longest waiting first). "Move up" / "Move down" in a card's or project's context menu (also Shift+F10 from the keyboard) do the same without dragging. "Toolkit: Reset session order" returns to automatic sorting. Cards show the time in that status, the last tool used ("after Bash"; only finished tool calls are recorded) or the tool asking for permission, and the last line of the last message. Click a card to focus its tab, in any VS Code window: each window lists the session tabs it opened in `~/.agent-status/windows/<pid>.json`, and a click on a session held by another window brings that window to the front (by opening its folder) and asks it, through `~/.agent-status/focus/<pid>.json`, to show the tab. A card's tooltip says where its session runs; a session started by hand outside the toolkit's tabs only gets a message. Hide a card with its eye icon until the session's next event; closing a tab hides its card too. A session whose Claude process has ended (tab, terminal or window closed, crash) disappears from the view, hidden group included; sessions recorded before the hook stored process ids fall back to the 6-hour cleanup. Hidden cards are listed in the collapsed "Hidden" group at the bottom of the view, where the eye button shows one again; hiding is remembered across reloads.

The hooks are installed with `node <clone>/status/install.mjs` (see [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)); it backs up `~/.claude/settings.json` first and adds only its own entries, and `--uninstall` removes them. A small synchronous start-up hook (`status/turn-status-hook.mjs`) asks every interactive session to end each turn with `STATUS: QUESTION` or `STATUS: DONE`. "Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup" opens a plain `claude` tab (session `<project>-claude`, no agent, plugin or prompt) whenever the folder opens; "Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" turns off both the plain tab and the coordinator for the folder.

The event hook (`status/status-hook.mjs`) runs asynchronously, so sessions never wait for it, and appends one line per event to `~/.agent-status/sessions/<session_id>.jsonl`; errors go to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`. It deletes a session's file at `SessionEnd` and leaves a `<session_id>.ended` marker so late background events cannot bring the session back (a new start or resume clears it), and, when a session starts, removes files and markers idle for more than 6 hours (`STALE_HOURS` at the top of the script). Headless sessions (`claude -p`, SDK, SDD's reviewer) are skipped by the observed but undocumented `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-*` value; `tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs` checks it against the installed CLI. A denied permission stays red until the turn ends, because Claude Code fires no event for a denial. To keep hooks light, no event is recorded after read-only tools (Read, Grep, Glob, LS, todo updates, tool search); if one of them asks for permission (for example a file outside the project), the card stays red after you grant it until the session's next command, edit or end of turn.

## Plugin delivery

The organization's managed Claude Code policy currently allows only the official Anthropic marketplace, so the plugin is loaded from the clone with `--plugin-dir` (the extension does it; by hand: `claude --plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit`). Update with `git pull`, then reload VS Code.

Once an admin allows the marketplace:

```
claude plugin marketplace add dserri/claude-toolkit
claude plugin install toolkit@claude-toolkit
```

and enable auto-update for `claude-toolkit` in `/plugin` → Marketplaces. The plugin declares no version, so every pushed commit is a release.

## Roll back

Delete the `dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1` junction and reload VS Code; remove a project's `.coord/` folder if you no longer want its board. Sessions started by hand work as before.

## Develop

```
node --test
node --test tests/coordinator.e2e.mjs tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs
```

The first runs the unit, hook, installer and `claude plugin validate` tests (`claude` must be on `PATH`). The second starts real headless sessions with a model call. Tab behaviour and the session view in VS Code are verified by hand.

# Design

## Context

Observed with probe hooks in headless sessions (Claude Code 2.1.326, Windows): hooks start as `claude → bash → bash → node`; a PostToolUse matcher `^(?!(Read|…)$).*` fires for `Bash` and not for `Read`; a Stop issued while a background shell runs carries `background_tasks: [{ id, type: "shell", status: "running", … }]`; when the task finishes, Claude starts a new turn (UserPromptSubmit with a new `prompt_id`) ending with a Stop whose `background_tasks` is empty.

## Decisions

- **Exclusion, not inclusion:** the matcher excludes known read-only tools, so any other tool, including future or MCP tools that may ask for permission, still clears a permission wait. `READ_ONLY_TOOLS` lives in the installer; the hook itself is unchanged for these events.
- **Installer replaces its own entries** (remove by command, then add), so matcher changes reach existing installs and the result stays idempotent.
- **Accepted limitation** (found in review): read-only tools can still ask for permission (paths outside the project); after the developer grants it no event is recorded, so the card stays red until the next recorded event (another tool, a permission, Stop). Rare in practice (reads inside the project need no permission, auto mode asks none) and short-lived; keeping their PostToolUse would undo most of the saving. Documented in README and pinned by a test.
- **Stuck threshold 15 minutes** in the setting default and the view's fallback.
- **Background status:** the hook records `background` = number of `background_tasks` with status `running` on Stop. The fold gives `question` if the agent asks, else `background` when that number is positive, else `finished`. `background` ranks with `working`, uses `charts.blue`, and the card reads "working in background · N task(s) · time". It is not subject to the stuck rule; the session's next event, its end, or its process ending clears it.

# Proposal

## Why

Measured on this machine: Claude Code runs every hook as `claude → bash → bash → node`, about 250 ms of CPU and roughly 60 MB for its short life, and the status hook ran on every tool call of every session. Most tool calls are read-only (Read, Grep, Glob), whose PostToolUse adds nothing the view needs. Separately, a session that ends its turn while a background task runs is shown yellow "finished" although it is still working.

## What Changes

- PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure status hooks are registered with a matcher that excludes read-only tools; re-running the installer updates existing installs.
- The "possibly stuck" default rises from 10 to 15 minutes, since read-only stretches no longer produce events.
- A Stop with running background tasks shows a new status "working in background", with its own colour and the number of tasks; it changes with the session's next event, including the turn Claude starts when a task finishes.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `session-status`: fewer hook processes, background status.

## Impact

`status/install.mjs`, `status/status-hook.mjs`, `vscode/status-core.js`, `vscode/package.json`, `vscode/sessions-view.js`, tests, README, INSTALL.md. Needs one installer rerun per machine.

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: No hook for read-only tools

The installer SHALL register the PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure status hooks with a matcher that excludes the read-only tools `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `LS`, `NotebookRead`, `TodoWrite`, `TodoRead` and `ToolSearch`, and re-running it SHALL update an existing install's matchers. The default "possibly stuck" threshold SHALL be 15 minutes.

#### Scenario: Reading files

- **WHEN** a session reads, greps and globs files
- **THEN** no status hook process starts for those calls

#### Scenario: Permission answered

- **WHEN** the developer grants a permission for a Bash, Edit, Write, web or MCP tool and it runs
- **THEN** the card returns from waiting for permission to working, as before

#### Scenario: Permission for a read-only tool

- **WHEN** a read-only tool such as Read asks for permission (for example outside the project) and the developer grants it
- **THEN** the card stays waiting for permission until the session's next recorded event (another tool, a new permission, the end of the turn); this delay is the accepted cost of not running the hook after read-only tools

#### Scenario: Upgrade

- **WHEN** the installer runs on a machine with the previous status hooks
- **THEN** the toolkit's entries carry the new matchers and no entry is duplicated

### Requirement: Background work

When a turn ends while background tasks are running and the agent does not ask the developer anything, the session SHALL show "working in background" with the number of running tasks, in its own colour, sorted with working sessions and never as possibly stuck. A turn ending with a question SHALL still show waiting for an answer.

#### Scenario: Background server

- **WHEN** a session starts a dev server in the background and ends its turn
- **THEN** its card shows "working in background · 1 task" instead of finished

#### Scenario: Task completes

- **WHEN** the background task finishes and Claude starts a new turn that ends with no running tasks
- **THEN** the card shows finished

# Tasks

## 1. Implementation

- [x] 1.1 Read-only exclusion matcher and own-entry replacement in `status/install.mjs`, with installer tests including the upgrade
- [x] 1.2 Record running background tasks on Stop in `status/status-hook.mjs`; `background` status in `status-core.js`; stuck default 15; tests
- [x] 1.3 README and INSTALL.md (colours, threshold, rerun the installer); rerun the installer on this machine

## 2. Acceptance

- [x] 2.1 With the developer: a session that starts a background process shows "working in background", then finished when it ends
